description: Three actual Raft instances: bootstrap v; elect v in term 2 and replicate its configuration/no-op; restart v and b; elect a in term 3 then restart a before its leader no-op; elect b in term 4 with a and self while dropping b-to-v vote RPC; replicate/commit b no-op to v but not a; restart b; in term 5 drop b-to-a vote RPC and optionally fail v candidate-key Set; finally actual a electSelf emits its term-5 stale-log request. Observe the v response for fault branch and no-failure control. Only the local freshness response is asserted.

harness.description: Actual runFollower, electSelf, requestVote, dispatchLogs, replicateTo and appendEntries with synchronous scheduled Transport and stable-store fault wrapper. Native vote requests read actual candidate logs. Stores survive selected node restarts.
semantic_changes: skipStartup suppresses autonomous background loops. The driver runs actual follower timeout and electSelf, drains all produced votes, and performs the same majority state transition as runCandidate; it does not implement a substitute vote handler.

Leader setup/no-op dispatch and actual replicateTo drive log prefix; driver executes source leaderLoop commit setters after actual commitment reaches the no-op. FSM consumption and independent timer races are not exercised.
Transport directly dispatches source processRPC. Exactly b-to-v term-4 and b-to-a term-5 RequestVote calls return scheduled loss; AppendEntries deliveries execute the real handler.
StableStore wrapper returns one candidate-key error before mutation; successful writes and restart state use the original InmemStore. The fault is injected only in one branch.
No later log overwrite or client endpoint is constructed or claimed; observing election counts is diagnostic, not a separate property.

legality.derivation: All candidate RequestVote messages come from electSelf reading actual local logs, and all grants come from requestVote. v term-2 leader initializes shared history. a receives v term-3 vote and restarts before leader work; b wins term 4 with a and self while its request to v is dropped. b then supplies a newer actual no-op to v, preserving v old vote for a. After b restart, its term-5 request to v has the same address as the known leader, so it passes that guard and advances v term; the one setter failure retains a from term 3. a never receives b term-5 request and therefore next electSelf legitimately requests term 5 with its older log. All campaign RPC results are drained before any restart or phase change. The no-failure control uses the same source prefix and deliveries. The precise fault is part of scope; no backend production failure frequency is inferred.
legality.applicability: One successful vote-term write and one no-write error from the candidate-key setter; later eligible candidate request with strictly older last-log term and no prior grant to that candidate in this term.

grounding.derivation: Correlate fixed case_id across the prefix and native response. The transport records the receiver live last entry before dispatch and candidate last-entry fields from the actual request, and calculates candidate_log_older from their terms. This observed antecedent independently establishes the unsafe eligibility condition; compare native response Granted with false. No result is suppressed based on Granted or the election tally. The control has no injected error and remains diagnostic.
grounding.applicability: One successful vote-term write and one no-write error from the candidate-key setter; later eligible candidate request with strictly older last-log term and no prior grant to that candidate in this term.

observable_properties.description: Under the scoped failed-write prefix, a candidate whose actual last-log term is older must not receive a new vote grant from this receiver.

uncertainties: The error-returning candidate write is a controlled StableStore substitute; no concrete production backend failure is exercised.
Main-loop election-result and commit-notification scheduling is explicit; autonomous timer races and FSM endpoints are outside the local handler claim.
